IBIS-ELECTRONICS EOOD (referred to below as the “Controller” or “Company”) operates in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act and Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to personal data processing and the free movement of such data. This information explains all aspects of the Company’s processing of your personal data and your related rights.
Legal basis for collecting, processing and storing your personal data
Article 1. The Controller collects and processes your personal data in connection with use of the online store
www.ibis-electronics.com
and the conclusion of contracts with the Company under Article 6(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), specifically on the following grounds:
Your express consent as a customer;
Performance of the Controller’s obligations under a contract with you;
Compliance with a legal obligation applicable to the Controller;
The legitimate interests of the Controller or a third party;
Purposes and principles of collecting, processing and storing your personal data
Article 2. (1) We collect and process the personal data you provide when using the online store and entering a contract with the Company, including for these purposes:
Creating an account and providing the full functionality of the online store;
Concluding and performing a distance contract;
Identifying a contracting party;
Accounting purposes;
Statistical purposes;
Protecting information security;
Ensuring performance of the contract for the relevant service.
Sending a newsletter at your request;
(2) We observe the following personal data processing principles:
Lawfulness, fairness and transparency;
Limitation of processing purposes;
Relevance to the processing purposes and minimisation of the data collected;
Accuracy and keeping data up to date;
Limitation of storage according to the purposes;
Integrity and confidentiality of processing and an appropriate level of personal data security.
(3) When processing and storing personal data, the Controller may also do so to protect these legitimate interests:
Fulfilling obligations to the National Revenue Agency, the Ministry of Interior and other state and municipal authorities.
Types of personal data collected, processed and stored by our Company
Article 3. (1) The Company carries out the following operations on the personal data you provide for these purposes:

User registration in the online store and performance of a distance sale contract: this creates an account to purchase goods through the online store and supplies contact details for delivering purchases. Registration and account creation are not mandatory for the service, which is largely available without an account.

Impact assessment conclusion: the assessment found that “User registration in the online store and performance of a distance sale contract” is permissible and provides sufficient safeguards for data subjects’ rights and legitimate interests under the GDPR.

Concluding and performing a commercial transaction with a customer or partner: this covers concluding, performing and administering the contract. Given the limited personal data collected and the use of publicly available sources for some of it, an impact assessment is not necessary for this operation.
Sending a newsletter: this administers newsletters to customers who have requested them. Given the limited personal data collected, an impact assessment is not necessary for this operation.

Exercising withdrawal rights or making a complaint: this administers the customer’s withdrawal or complaint. Given the limited personal data collected, an impact assessment is not necessary for this operation.
(2) The Controller processes the following categories of personal data and information for these purposes and on these grounds:
Your identifying details (email, name and others)
Purpose of collection: 1) Contacting the user and sending information; 2) Registering the user in the online store; 3) Sending a newsletter.

Legal basis: accepting the General Terms and Conditions and registering, ordering without registration, or concluding a written contract creates a contractual relationship between you and the Controller, on which processing is based under Article 6(1)(b) GDPR. Newsletter details are processed on your express consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR.
Delivery details (names, phone, address and others)
Purpose of collection: performance of the Controller’s obligations under the sale and delivery contract for the purchased goods.

Legal basis: accepting the General Terms and Conditions and registering, ordering without registration, or concluding a written contract creates a contractual relationship between you and the Controller, on which processing is based under Article 6(1)(b) GDPR.
Additional details you provide: you may supplement your account with your first name, last name and phone number.
Purpose of collection: supplementing the user’s account information.

Legal basis: you gave express consent to processing for one or more specific purposes under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR when registering in the online store. Providing these details is not mandatory for registration.
(3) The Controller does not collect or process personal data concerning the following:
Racial or ethnic origin;
Political, religious or philosophical beliefs, or trade union membership;
Genetic or biometric data, health data, or data about sex life or sexual orientation.
(4) The Controller collects personal data from the individuals to whom it relates.
(5) The Company does not carry out automated decision-making using data.
Article 4. (1) The Company carries out the following operations on the personal data you provide as legal representatives or authorised agents of corporate business partners, for these purposes:

Concluding and performing a commercial transaction: we process only the full name of the legal representative or authorised person to conclude and perform a transaction with a commercial company. Impact assessment conclusion: given the small number of individuals and the limited personal data collected, an impact assessment is not necessary for this operation.
(2) The Controller collects the personal data from the individuals concerned and from the Commercial Register maintained by the Registry Agency.
(3) The Company does not carry out automated decision-making using data.

Article 5. The Controller may use “cookies” to provide full website functionality, improve the user experience, compile statistics, facilitate access and for other purposes, to which you agree by using our website. You may control and/or delete cookies at any time through your browser settings. Cookies are not personal data and are not used to identify visitors or users of the online store.
Personal data retention period

Article 6. (1) The Controller retains personal data for no longer than the existence of your online store account. After account deletion, the Controller takes the necessary care to erase and destroy all your data without undue delay or anonymise it so that it no longer identifies you.

(2) The Controller processes the personal data provided when ordering without registration until completion of the order, unless you expressly consented when ordering to processing for service improvement, recommended content, individual terms, promotions or statistical purposes.
(3) The Controller retains personal data supplied for online orders for five years to protect its legal interests in judicial or administrative disputes with online store users.
(4) The Controller informs you if retention must be extended to comply with a statutory obligation, for its legitimate interests or for another reason.
(5) The Controller retains personal data required by applicable law for the prescribed period, which may exceed the existence of your online store account or completion of the order.

Article 7. The Controller retains business partners’ legal representatives’ personal data during contract performance and for its legitimate interests and legal obligations. This period may exceed the contract’s term.
Disclosure of your personal data for processing

Article 8. (1) The Controller may, at its discretion, disclose some or all personal data to processors to fulfil the processing purposes you have agreed to, in compliance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).
(2) The Controller informs you if it intends to transfer some or all personal data to third countries or international organisations.
Your rights concerning the collection, processing and storage of personal data
Withdrawing consent to personal data processing

Article 9. (1) If you no longer wish your data to be processed for marketing and newsletters, you may withdraw consent at any time by emailing the consent withdrawal form in Appendix 1 or a free-text request.

(2) After receiving your request, we email the address you supplied for newsletters and advertising with detailed instructions to verify you as the newsletter recipient and the data subject concerned.
(3) Withdrawal of consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal.
Right of access
Article 10. (1) You may request and receive confirmation whether the Controller processes personal data about you by emailing a free-text request.
(2) You may access the data relating to you and information about its collection, processing and storage.
(3) After receiving the request, we email the address you used to register or order with detailed instructions to verify you as the data subject requesting access.
(4) Following verification under paragraph 3, the Controller provides, on request, a copy of your processed personal data in electronic or another appropriate form.
(5) Access is free, but the Controller reserves the right to charge an administrative fee for repetitive or excessive requests.
Right to rectification or completion
Article 11. (1) You may correct or complete inaccurate or incomplete personal data at any time through “Edit account”.
(2) You may do so directly through your account or by emailing the Controller using the form in Appendix 4 or a free-text request.
Right to erasure (“right to be forgotten”)
Article 12. (1) You may request erasure of some or all personal data relating to you, and the Controller must erase it without undue delay where any of these grounds applies:
The data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected or otherwise processed;
You withdraw the consent on which processing is based and there is no other legal basis;
You object to processing, including for direct marketing, and there are no overriding legitimate grounds;
The personal data was processed unlawfully;
The data must be erased to comply with an EU or Member State legal obligation applicable to the Controller;
The data was collected in connection with offering information society services.
(2) The Controller need not erase data where it is stored and processed:
To exercise freedom of expression and information;
To comply with an EU or Member State legal obligation applicable to the Controller, or to perform a task in the public interest or exercise official authority vested in it;
For public interest reasons in public health;
For archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes;
To establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

(3) To exercise the right to be forgotten, email the form in Appendix 2 or a free-text erasure request. The Controller then emails the address used to register or order with detailed instructions to verify you as the store user and data subject requesting erasure.
(4) Once we verify that the requester and data subject are the same person under those instructions, we erase all data processed about you in accordance with paragraph 3.
(5) If an order is being processed, the earliest time you can request to be “forgotten” is after the order is successfully completed.
Right to restriction
Article 13. You may request restriction of processing by emailing a free-text request where:
You contest the accuracy of personal data, for a period allowing the Controller to verify it;
Processing is unlawful but you request restriction of use instead of erasure;
The Controller no longer needs the data for processing, but you need it to establish, exercise or defend legal claims;
You have objected to processing pending verification whether the Controller’s legitimate grounds override your interests.
(2) After receiving the request, we email the address used to register or order with detailed instructions to verify you as the store user and data subject requesting restriction.
(3) Following verification under paragraph 2, the Company stops processing your data but does not remove any posts you have made in the online store.
Right to data portability
Article 14. (1) If you consented to processing, processing is necessary for the contract with the Controller, or your data is processed automatically, you may:
Ask the Controller to provide your personal data in a readable format and transfer it to another controller;
Ask the Controller to transfer it directly to a controller you specify where technically feasible.

(2) To exercise portability, email the completed form in Appendix 3 or a free-text request. The Controller then emails the address used to register or order with detailed instructions to verify you as the store user and data subject requesting portability.
(3) Following verification under paragraph 2, the Company sends the data it processes about you to your specified email address in XML format.
Right to receive information

Article 15. You may ask the Controller to identify all recipients to whom data subject to rectification, erasure or restriction requests has been disclosed. The Controller may refuse if this would be impossible or involve disproportionate effort.
Right to object
Article 16. You may object at any time to the Controller’s processing of personal data relating to you, including profiling or direct marketing.
Your rights in the event of a personal data breach

Article 17. (1) If the Controller identifies a personal data breach likely to present a high risk to your rights and freedoms, it informs you without undue delay of the breach and measures taken or planned.
(2) The Controller need not notify you if:
It has applied appropriate technical and organisational protections to the affected data;
It has subsequently taken measures ensuring that the breach will not create a high risk to your rights;
Notification would involve disproportionate effort.
Recipients of your personal data
Article 18. (1) To process your data, provide full service functionality and serve your interests, the Controller may disclose data to the following processors:
Personal data processor — Purpose of personal data processing
(2) Processors comply with all lawfulness and security requirements when processing and storing your data.
Article 19. The Controller does not transfer your data to third countries.
Article 20. If your rights under the above provisions or applicable data protection law are infringed, you may complain to the Commission for Personal Data Protection as follows:

Article 22. If consent relates to a transfer, the Controller describes the possible risks of transfer to third countries in the absence of an adequacy decision and appropriate safeguards.
